articles.headline: Sanofi's $41B Insmed buy biggest since Pfizer/Seagen
articles.summary: Sanofi is acquiring Insmed for approximately $41 billion, marking the largest biopharma deal since Pfizer's acquisition of Seagen. The deal gives Sanofi access to Insmed's two commercial products — including treprostinil for nontuberculous mycobacterial lung disease (NTMBC) — and a broader pipeline in immunology and rare disease, areas Sanofi is prioritizing as it looks to diversify away from its legacy portfolio. Sanofi characterized the deal as 'transformative,' signaling continued big-pharma appetite for durable rare-disease franchises with strong pricing power.
articles.why_it_matters: This landmark deal reshapes the rare-disease competitive landscape and sets a valuation benchmark for similar pipeline assets, with immediate implications for INSM shareholders and sector positioning in immunology and orphan drug M&A.

articles.headline: What to expect in US healthcare in 2027 and beyond
articles.summary: McKinsey's annual US healthcare outlook maps the structural forces reshaping the sector through 2027, including Medicaid work requirements rollout, Medicare Advantage star-rating overhaul, payer margin pressure, and AI adoption curves across provider and payer segments. It synthesizes regulatory, demographic, and technology trends into a single forward-looking framework. The piece is particularly useful for calibrating healthcare sector exposure ahead of significant policy inflection points.
articles.why_it_matters: With Medicaid and Medicare Advantage policy shifts creating meaningful earnings risk for managed care and provider companies, this framework helps investors size exposure and anticipate which sub-sectors face headwinds versus tailwinds into 2027.
